sections.label: Nominee shareholder register amendments
sections.summary: Amendments require local and foreign companies to keep a non-public register of nominee shareholders and nominators, updated within seven days.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: The first set of amendments today aims to address these concerns and align our legislation with FATF recommendations, by requiring both local and foreign companies in Singapore to, first, keep a non-public register of nominee shareholders and their nominators; and second, to update their register within seven days of being informed by the nominee.

sections.label: Identifying registrable controllers
sections.summary: Companies and LLPs unable to identify a registrable controller must identify all individuals with executive control as registrable controllers.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Under the new requirement, companies and LLPs which are unable to identify a registrable controller who has a significant interest in or significant control over the company or LLP will be required to identify all individuals with executive control over the company or LLP as registrable controllers.

sections.label: Register of Nominee Directors updates
sections.summary: Local companies must update their Register of Nominee Directors within seven days of receiving information from nominee directors.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: The third set of amendments requires local companies to update their Register of Nominee Directors within seven days of receiving information from their nominee directors.

sections.label: Clarify executive control listing
sections.summary: The question asks the Minister to clarify why directors with executive control and the CEO must be listed if no registrable controller is identified.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: First, can the Minister clarify the reasons why directors with executive control and the CEO must be listed in the register if no registrable controller is identified?

sections.label: Clarify nominee shareholders definition
sections.summary: The question asks the Minister to provide more clarity on the definition of nominee shareholders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Second, can Minister provide more clarity on the definition of "nominee shareholders"?

sections.label: Support for small businesses
sections.summary: The question asks how the Ministry will support small businesses in complying with the new regulations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Third and finally, can the Ministry share how it will support small businesses in complying with these new regulations?

sections.label: Nominee director register update deadlines
sections.summary: The Bill would require local companies to update nominee director registers within seven days, and foreign companies may update member registers within 30 days.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The amendment Bill, if passed, will result in local companies having to update their register of nominee directors within seven days, instead of the 14 days under section 173A of the Companies Act, while foreign companies may update their register of members within 30 days.

sections.label: Consultation feedback on 14-day timeline
sections.summary: Consultation feedback proposed local companies be given 14 days, aligning with section 173A of the Companies Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: With that being said, feedback from the consultation proposed that local companies should be given 14 days instead, as this would be line with section 173A of the Companies Act – which will really require a company to provide updates regarding changes to any appointment of directors, chief executive officer, secretaries, auditors and others within the period of 14 days.

sections.label: Two timelines for local companies
sections.summary: If accepted, local companies would have two timelines, while foreign companies would be uniformly subject to one timeline.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Should this provision be accepted by this House, there would be two timelines for local companies, in contrast to foreign companies being uniformly subject to one timeline.

sections.label: Clarifications on FATF Recommendations
sections.summary: The passage asks how the Government intends to improve compliance with FATF Recommendations 22, 28 and 35, and when MOF and ACRA will provide clarifications.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Given that it is ostensibly the goal of this Bill to counter money laundering and terrorism financing concerns and recognising the increasingly sophisticated methods employed to launder money and finance terror activities, how does the Government intend to improve compliance with these three FATF Recommendations 22, 28 and 35?

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In their document published in response to key feedback received for this Bill, MOF and ACRA have stated that such terms are "to be clarified".

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: As such, could the Minister advise when MOF and ACRA intend to provide such clarifications?

sections.label: Executive powers where no controllers
sections.summary: Where no registrable controllers are identified, persons with executive powers within the company are effectively exercising control.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: In situations where no registrable controllers are identified, persons with executive powers within the company are effectively exercising control.

sections.label: Nominee dividends and listed companies exemption
sections.summary: It would suffice if the nominee is expected to receive dividends on behalf of the nominator, and listed public companies and their shareholders are not subject to the new requirement.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Practically, it would suffice if the nominee is expected to receive the dividends on behalf of the nominator, even if the dividends are not eventually distributed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: I would also add that public companies listed in Singapore and their shareholders will not be subject to this new requirement, as provided for in the Fourteenth Schedule of the Companies Act.

sections.label: New requirements for companies and LLPs
sections.summary: The passage states the new requirements are unlikely to increase compliance cost and will apply only to companies and LLPs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Again, this is unlikely to increase compliance cost.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: I would also like to highlight that these new requirements will only apply to companies and LLPs.

sections.label: Reviewing regulations for international alignment
sections.summary: The passage states regulations and practices are continually reviewed to align with international practices and frameworks, with some matters taking more time.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The answer is that we continually review our regulations and our practices to make sure that we are in line with international practices.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Some things may take a little bit more time while some things need to be studied.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: So, for example, this latest set of amendments are a result of our review coming out of previous comments.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: But I think the Member can be assured that we will continue to work towards greater transparency and making sure that we are in alignment with international frameworks.
